title: Copilot Studio: discover and use shared plugins from Microsoft's plugin registry
summary: Hold: the data-policy automation only reads a policy; it cannot block a connector. The briefing also labels licensing as unpublished despite documented product licensing, and casts doubt on data-policy coverage that Microsoft states applies to Copilot Studio agents.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans a connection between Copilot Studio and Microsoft's shared plugin registry.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio now connects to Microsoft's shared plugin registry

claims.claim: The planned connection makes it easier for makers to discover and use plugins, connectors and other capabilities.
claims.quote: making it easier for makers to discover and use plugins, connectors, and other available capabilities

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: Administrators manage plugins in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Admins manage plugins, including the skills and MCP servers they contain, in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described how registry-discovered plugins appear in the Copilot Studio maker experience.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio shared plugin registry discover use plugins enable admin switch default maker experience identity harness'; opened add-tools-custom-agent and plugins/overview. Neither describes a registry-plugin discovery screen in Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described how plugins discovered through this registry are attached to a Copilot Studio agent.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio shared plugin registry maker discover plugins approval default identity harness integration 570669'; opened add-tools-custom-agent, plugins/overview and govern-plugins. No registry-plugin attachment procedure was found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed the approval flow for this specific Copilot Studio integration.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio shared plugin registry maker discover plugins approval default identity harness integration 570669'; opened govern-plugins and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers. They document plugin and MCP approvals, not this integration's approval flow.

claims.claim: Package approval does not replace Power Platform policies.
claims.quote: Package approval doesn't replace Power Platform policies or service permissions.

claims.claim: The checked sources do not state that the integration changes existing behaviour automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio shared plugin registry discover use plugins enable admin switch default maker experience identity harness'; read roadmap, add-tools-custom-agent and plugins/overview. Found no automatic replacement or change to existing agents.

claims.claim: Plugin tools can connect to apps and data through Copilot connectors and remote MCP integrations.
claims.quote: Tools | Connect to apps and data, including supported Copilot connectors and remote MCP integrations.

claims.claim: Users might still need to sign in, grant consent or configure a service connection after plugin installation.
claims.quote: Users might still need to sign in, grant consent, or configure a service connection after installation, depending on the component and product.

claims.claim: Plugin approval does not replace connected-service permissions or connection setup.
claims.quote: Approval grants access to the requested plugin; it doesn't replace permissions or connection setup required by its connected services.

claims.claim: An approved MCP server becomes available to agent-building surfaces only after Microsoft Entra consent.
claims.quote: After approval, consent to the Microsoft Entra permissions required by the MCP server. The server becomes available to agent-building surfaces only after consent is granted.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified the runtime identity for plugins obtained through this particular registry integration.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio registry plugins authentication identity user maker credentials consent'; opened add-tools-custom-agent and govern-plugins; reviewed identity and credential search excerpts. They describe existing tool authentication, not this registry integration.

claims.claim: The plugin catalog can include third-party and Microsoft-published plugins.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio shared plugin registry maker discover plugins approval default identity harness integration 570669'; opened add-tools-custom-agent and plugins/overview. Existing tool defaults are documented, but their mapping to this integration is not.

claims.quote: After approval and consent, the MCP server can take up to 30 minutes to appear in all Microsoft Copilot Studio environments in the tenant.

claims.claim: The roadmap record names no licence or meter specific to this feature.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Scope: which licences makers need

claims.quote: To use Copilot Studio, you need one of the following configurations: ... Copilot Studio user license (free). ... Copilot Studio authors role in Power Platform admin center. ... Microsoft 365 Copilot license ... Copilot Studio trial license.

Replace Scope's 'which licences makers need' with 'whether an additional registry-specific licence is needed'. In Cost and licensing add: 'Copilot Studio has documented authoring access and Copilot Credits licensing; follow the licensing guidance for the agent harness. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing and https://learn.microsoft.com/plugins/cost-considerations#check-product-specific-licensing-and-billing.

claims.claim: Get-DlpPolicy -PolicyName <policy name> is the automation counterpart for controlling which connectors and tools makers can use.
claims.quote: Retrieves a list of DLP policy objects. ... The Get-DlpPolicy cmdlet retrieves policy objects for the logged in admin's tenant.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].api.call and the rendered call with 'Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy GUID> -Connectors <connector objects> -Classification Blocked' and its docs URL with https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powerapps.administration.powershell/add-connectorstopolicy. Replace the read-only note with 'The call moves the specified connectors to the Blocked group; each connector object requires id, type and name.' This reference explicitly documents the move and the Blocked classification. Keep inventory advice separate from the setting call.

claims.claim: The currently printed Get-DlpPolicy call reads a policy rather than changing it.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Power Platform data policies control which tools makers can add to Copilot Studio agents in scoped environments.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope. ... To prevent agent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Whether Power Platform data policies cover registry-sourced capabilities used in Copilot Studio agents is unconfirmed.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope. ... Data policies and sharing rules that apply to a Copilot Studio agent continue to apply when the agent is packaged in a plugin.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket data-policy caveat in controls[1].note, Risk assessment and the risk rationale with: 'Data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments in scope and govern Power Platform connector tools, not Copilot connectors. How the shared-registry experience maps plugin capabilities to those connectors is not yet documented.' Narrow the corresponding Open question to: 'How does the shared-registry experience map plugin capabilities to Power Platform connectors and data groups?' Use https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention; do not imply that an undocumented discovery route exempts agent tools from existing policies.

claims.quote: Install and uninstall | Selected plugin or standalone skill package. | Install the package for users without requiring manual installation by end users, or uninstall a previously installed package.

claims.claim: Blocking a plugin package also blocks its included agents.

claims.claim: Associated MCP servers and connectors remain available to other plugins, so a package block need not block the connector itself.

claims.claim: The connector tools governed by Copilot Studio data policies are Power Platform connectors, not Copilot connectors.
claims.quote: Power Platform connectors refers to Power Platform connectors used as tools in an agent. They don't refer to Copilot connectors.
